claims.claim: Appointed Sporting head coach on 26 December 2024, succeeding João Pereira, from Vitória de Guimarães
claims.note: A BOLA article dated 26 Dec 2024 reports the official appointment and that V. Guimarães confirmed his departure.

claims.claim: Sporting paid Vitória SC a fee of 4,100,000 euros
Contract valid to 30 June 2026 with option to 30 June 2027 (first report)
Four staff moved from Guimarães under the deal, including two assistant coaches
claims.note: Two assistant coaches plus Fernando Alves and José Pedro Lage.

claims.claim: Born or coaching start in Mirandela; Mirandela called his home town; began coaching there after ending his playing career
claims.note: RTP calls Mirandela his 'cidade natal' and says he began coaching there after ending playing career. Country not stated; not repeated in the body.

claims.claim: Académico de Viseu: kept out of relegation in 2018/19; Taça semi-final 2019/20 lost to FC Porto
Académica fourth in 2020/21, matching best season since leaving top flight in 2015/16
Nacional sixth in 2021/22, frustration at missing promotion
Vilafranquense fifth at 19th matchday; Mafra 14th to sixth in last 14 rounds
Joined Moreirense July 2023; 55 points in 34 matchdays, sixth; 16 matchdays without conceding; played there 2007/08 and 2008/09; extended contract to 2026
Presented by Vitória de Guimarães on 28 May 2024; sixth with 23 points after 15 matchdays in 2024/25; Portuguese record of nine consecutive UEFA wins
claims.note: Stated in RTP profile; the record is placed in the article's Vitória section, which is written before his Sporting move.

claims.claim: Sporting appointment followed Rúben Amorim's departure and João Pereira's spell of about a month
claims.note: RTP says the appointment was to succeed Amorim (left for Manchester United) and Pereira, whose spell lasted about a month.

claims.claim: Sporting won the 2024/25 Liga Portugal, the club's 21st league title
claims.note: Soccerway report of the award states the 21st title.

claims.claim: Voted best coach 2024/25 by the league's coaches and captains; gala at LPFP headquarters in Porto

claims.note: Profile field NACIONALIDADE reads Portugal. Liga Portugal is a league source.

claims.claim: Contract runs to June 2028 with option for one more year (27 Oct 2026 report)
claims.note: Stated in A Bola report; conflict with the 2024 report is disclosed in the body.

claims.claim: 27 Oct 2026: position at risk; Sporting lost 1-2 at home to Académico de Viseu; Marítimo match could be last; wins would only postpone an exit
claims.note: All stated in the A Bola article. The date is the article date.

claims.claim: 29 Oct 2026: Sporting's coach spoke publicly; A Bola reported his remarks
claims.note: The article reports his remarks. The page does not name the setting or the match, so the body says nothing about either.
